It can be calculated by comparing the price of that diamond to that of the other diamonds in the market. The Price List can be accessed by members only.

title: What’s the best vegetarian alternative to gelatine?
summary: “The truth is, there’s no exact substitute for gelatine, because it has an incredibly unique texture,” says Richard Phillips, head of pastry at Timberyard in Edinburgh. Sure, there are plenty of plant-based gelling agents out there – “agar-agar [or just agar], gellan gum, pectin, carrageenan, locust bean gum, vege-gel... the list goes on,” says Phillips – but the result will never quite be the same. “The temperature you have to use them at is different [to gelatin],” says Philip Khoury, author of Beyond Baking, so his usual workaround is to simply formulate recipes that don’t use gelling agent.
